verdict.rationale: First-party docs mention 'EU regional subusers', and a long-time user reports running 'one main account, 3 sub-accounts', so SendGrid has its own subuser/sub-account construct. Community evidence also says it is easy to send on behalf of clients with passing SPF/DKIM, alongside documented domain authentication. However, nothing documents what is actually isolated per tenant. missing for 10: documentation of per-subuser API credentials, separate suppression lists, isolated sender reputation/IPs, multi-domain-per-tenant management, and subuser provisioning APIs.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I can isolate tenants — subaccounts, subusers, or multiple domains with separate credentials, suppression lists, and reputation — for the platform I'm building

citations.quote: Base url: https://api.eu.sendgrid.com (for EU regional subusers)
my accounts (one main account, 3 sub-accounts) were not put under review
One thing Sendgrid is good at is letting people easily send emails on behalf of their clients while still passing SPF/DKIM checks
Domain authentication verifies the legitimacy of your email servers, messages, and sending addresses.
